title: System Log 1: The for Loop
lessonSummary: Time loop mastered! A for loop repeats code for every step of range().

tasks.instruction: Run this example: a for loop with range(5).
tasks.codeTemplate:
for i in range(5):
    print(f"Time Cycle {i+1}: Systems synchronized")

tasks.instruction: Use a for loop with range(3) and print the lines Cycle 1: online, Cycle 2: online and Cycle 3: online (print i+1).
Use a for loop with range(4) and print Engine 0: ready up to Engine 3: ready (print i itself, it starts at 0).

title: System Log 2: range() with Start, End and Step
lessonSummary: Precision achieved! range() can start anywhere and skip sectors.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: scan sectors 3 to 7, then reinforce every second sector.
Use range(3, 7) and print Sector 3: scanned up to Sector 6: scanned.
Use range(2, 11, 2) and print Pulse 2, Pulse 4 and so on up to Pulse 10.

title: System Log 3: Counting Backwards
lessonSummary: Countdown complete! A negative step makes range() count backwards.

tasks.instruction: Run the hyperspace countdown.
Count down from 3 to 1 with range(3, 0, -1). Print T-minus 3, T-minus 2, T-minus 1 and then (after the loop) Lift-off!
Use range(10, 0, -3) and print Level 10, Level 7, Level 4 and Level 1. Then print Done after the loop.

title: System Log 4: Loops over Strings
lessonSummary: Code decoded letter by letter! A for loop can walk through any text.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: the letters of the code ALPHA.
tasks.codeTemplate:
code = "ALPHA"
print(f"The code is: {code}")
print("Letter by letter:")
for letter in code:
    print(f"  - {letter}")

tasks.instruction: Create code = "NEXUS" and print every letter in the format Letter: N, Letter: E and so on (last line: Letter: S).
Create code = "QUANTUM". Count its letters with a variable count (start at 0, add 1 per letter) and print exactly: Letters: 7

title: System Log 5: The while Loop
lessonSummary: Scanner running! A while loop repeats as long as its condition is true.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: scan from 0 to 10.
tasks.codeTemplate:
scan = 0
while scan <= 10:
    print(f"Scan {scan}: Data received")
    scan += 1
print("Scan finished")

tasks.instruction: Create count = 3. While count > 0 print Ignition in 3, Ignition in 2, Ignition in 1 (do not forget to reduce count by 1 in the loop).
Create energy = 100. While energy > 20 subtract 15 and print Energy: 85%, Energy: 70% and so on. The last line must read: Energy: 10%

title: System Log 6: while with Counters
lessonSummary: Shield under control! Counters inside a while loop track time and values.

tasks.instruction: Run the shield generator.
tasks.codeTemplate:
energy = 100
minute = 1
while energy > 20:
    consumption = 15
    energy -= consumption
    print(f"Minute {minute}: -{consumption} energy, remaining: {energy}%")
    minute += 1
print(f"Shield critical after {minute-1} minutes!")

tasks.instruction: Create fuel = 50 and minute = 1. While fuel >= 12 subtract 12 and print Minute 1: fuel 38, Minute 2: fuel 26 and so on (increase minute each pass). The last line must read: Minute 4: fuel 2
Create signal = 1. While signal < 100 double it (signal *= 2) and print Signal: 2, Signal: 4 and so on. The last line must read: Signal: 128

title: System Log 7: Nested Loops
lessonSummary: Time within time! The inner loop runs completely on every pass of the outer loop.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: scan all decks and print a hologram pattern.
Use two nested loops: decks 1 to 2 (range(1, 3)) and rooms 1 to 3. Print one line per room in the format Deck 1, room 1. The last line must read: Deck 2, room 3
Print a block of * with 3 rows and 4 columns (nested loops, print("*", end="") and an empty print() after each row). The output must be exactly four stars per row on three lines.

title: Debug Quest
lessonSummary: All bugs found! Loops need the right range, a colon and the correct indentation.

tasks.instruction: 🐛 Bug #1 – Goal: The program should count the time from 1 to 5 and print each value (Time 1 up to Time 5). What is wrong?
🐛 Bug #2 – Goal: The program should print System 1 through System 5. What is wrong?
🐛 Bug #3 – Goal: The program should print Log 0, Log 1 and Log 2 and then print End once. What is wrong?

title: Mission 1: The Quantum Counter
lessonSummary: Quantum counter calibrated – you master counting patterns!

tasks.instruction: Step 1 – Print all numbers from 1 to 20 with a for loop in the format Time: 1, Time: 2 and so on (the last line must read: Time: 20).
Step 2 – First print the even numbers 2 to 20 as Even: 2 … Even: 20. Then print the numbers 20 down to 1 as Countdown: 20 … Countdown: 1 and after the loop the line Liftoff!
Step 3 – Calculate the sum of all numbers from 1 to 100 with a loop (variable total, start at 0) and print exactly: Sum: 5050

title: Mission 2: The Space Station Commander
lessonSummary: Station under control – every deck checked!

tasks.instruction: Step 1 – Go through the decks 1 to 10 and print Deck 1: OK, Deck 2: OK and so on (the last line must read: Deck 10: OK).

Step 2 – Extend the loop: for each deck print Deck N: OK. Additionally print ⚠️ Warning on Deck N for the decks 3, 6 and 9 (use if with or) and Bonus on Deck N for the decks 5 and 10. Check: the last line of the whole output must read: Bonus on Deck 10

Step 3 – Deck 7 is under maintenance: for Deck 7 print only Deck 7 under maintenance (instead of Deck 7: OK), all other decks 1 to 10 print Deck N: OK. After the loop print ✅ All important decks checked!

title: Mission 3: The Time Paradox
lessonSummary: Paradox solved – you found your way back through time!

tasks.instruction: Step 1 – Create year = 2100 and jumps = 0. While year != 2000 jump back 25 years (year -= 25), increase jumps by 1 and print Jump 1: year 2075, Jump 2: year 2050 and so on. The last line must read: Jump 4: year 2000
Step 2 – Create year = 2000 and jumps = 0. While jumps < 5 jump forward 30 years and count the jump. After the loop print exactly: Final year: 2150 and Trapped in the time paradox

validation.expected:
Final year: 2150
Trapped in the time paradox

tasks.instruction: Step 3 – Print a status report only for every third jump of 1 to 9: use range(1, 10, 3) and print Status: jump 1, Status: jump 4, Status: jump 7.

title: Extra challenge 1: The Prime Number Decryption
lessonSummary: Codes decrypted – you found every prime number!

tasks.instruction: Step 1 – Prepare the number range: go through the numbers 2 to 20 and print Testing 2 … Testing 20 (the last line must read: Testing 20).

Step 2 – Test the single number 15: create number = 15 and is_prime = True. Use two nested loops over a and b (both range(2, number)); if a * b == number set is_prime = False. Print exactly: 15 is prime: False
Step 3 – Test all numbers 2 to 30 the same way. Print every prime as Prime: 2, Prime: 3 … and count them in a variable found (start at 0). After the loop print exactly: Primes found: 10
Step 4 – Visualise the numbers 2 to 30 in one line: for a prime print P, otherwise a dot . (use print(..., end="") and an empty print() at the end). Expected line: PP.P.P...P.P...P.P...P.....P.

title: Extra challenge 2: The Holodeck
lessonSummary: Holodeck online – grid, pattern and target under control!

tasks.instruction: Step 1 – Build the holodeck grid with two nested loops: 8 rows, 8 columns. Print a dot . for every field (print(".", end="") and an empty print() after each row). Expected: eight dots per row on eight lines.

Step 2 – Draw the chessboard pattern: create dark = True. For every field print # if dark is True, otherwise a dot; then flip dark (dark = not dark). After each row print a line break and flip dark once more. The first two rows must read #.#.#.#. and .#.#.#.#

Step 3 – Simulate movement: create player_row = 1 and player_col = 1. While player_row < 8 move diagonally (add 1 to both) and print Player on field 2, 2 and so on. The last line must read: Player on field 8, 8
Step 4 – Check the target: extend Step 3 with target_row = 8 and target_col = 8. After the loop check with if and and whether the player is on the target and print exactly: 🎯 Target reached!

title: Extra challenge 3: The Endless Tunnel
lessonSummary: 🎊 Congratulations! You have mastered Week 4 – next up is Week 5: Functions (def, return)!

tasks.instruction: Step 1 – Program the tunnel loop: create distance = 0. While distance < 10 add 1 and print Portal 1 passed, Portal 2 passed and so on. The last line must read: Portal 10 passed

Step 2 – Add ship values: fuel = 100 and shield = 60. While fuel > 0 and shield > 0 pass one portal (distance += 1), subtract 20 fuel and 8 shield and print Portal 1: fuel 80, shield 52 and so on. The last line must read: Portal 5: fuel 0, shield 20
Step 3 – After the loop of Step 2 print exactly: Tunnel ended after 5 portals and, with if, the reason: Reason: out of fuel (if fuel <= 0).

validation.expected:
Tunnel ended after 5 portals
Reason: out of fuel

tasks.instruction: Step 4 – Find the best flight: test the fuel use per portal 10, 20 and 30 (for fuel_use in range(10, 31, 10)). For each flight start again with fuel = 100, shield = 60, distance = 0 and fly with the while loop (subtract fuel_use fuel and 8 shield per portal). Keep the largest distance in best_distance (start at 0) and print at the end exactly: Best distance: 8
